scenes.say: Why does a 4 to 20 milliamp signal start at 4, and not at zero?
scenes.html:
Explainer
Why does 4–20 mA
start at 4?
Syon Automation LLC

scenes.say: Because zero has to mean something is wrong.
scenes.html:
The short answer
Zero has to mean
something is wrong.
Syon Automation LLC

scenes.say: Four to twenty milliamps has been the workhorse of process instruments for decades: pressure, level, flow and temperature transmitters.
scenes.html:
The workhorse signal
Pressure · Level
Flow · Temperature
One analog signal for decades of plant instruments
Syon Automation LLC

scenes.say: Four milliamps is the bottom of the range, zero percent. Twenty milliamps is the top, one hundred percent.
scenes.html:
The range
4 mA = 0% · 20 mA = 100%
Syon Automation LLC

scenes.say: If a wire breaks or the transmitter loses power, the current falls toward zero. The PLC sees less than 4 milliamps and knows it's a fault, not a real reading. That's called a live zero.
scenes.html:
A live zero
Broken wire → near 0 mA
The PLC knows it's a fault, not a reading.
Syon Automation LLC

scenes.say: Those 4 milliamps can also power the transmitter itself, so a two-wire loop carries power and signal on the same pair.
scenes.html:
Power and signal on one pair
Syon Automation LLC

scenes.say: Why current and not voltage? In a series loop the current is the same everywhere, so long wire runs don't change the reading, and it holds up better against electrical noise.
scenes.html:
Why current, not voltage
Same current
at every point
Long runs don't change the reading. Better noise immunity.
Syon Automation LLC

scenes.say: Many instruments follow NAMUR N E 43. Readings from 3.8 to 20.5 milliamps are measurements. At or below 3.6, or at or above 21, the transmitter is signaling a failure.
scenes.html:
NAMUR NE 43
3.8 – 20.5 mA
measurement
≤ 3.6 or ≥ 21 mA
failure signal
Source: NAMUR NE 43 signal levels
Syon Automation LLC

scenes.say: Scaling is a straight line. Percent equals the reading minus 4, divided by 16, times 100. So 12 milliamps is 50 percent.
scenes.html:
Scaling
% = (mA − 4) ÷ 16 × 100
12 mA → 50%
Syon Automation LLC

scenes.say: Example: a level transmitter ranged zero to ten feet reads 16 milliamps. 16 minus 4 is 12, divided by 16 is 75 percent, so the level is seven and a half feet.
scenes.html:
Worked example
Range 0–10 ft · reading 16 mA
(16 − 4) ÷ 16 = 75%
= 7.5 ft
Syon Automation LLC

scenes.say: Many transmitters also carry HART, a digital signal riding on the same pair, for setup and diagnostics.
scenes.html:
Bonus: HART
Digital data
on the same pair
for setup and diagnostics
Syon Automation LLC

scenes.say: Troubleshooting tip: measure the loop current with a meter in series, and compare it to what the PLC shows. If they disagree, look at the scaling or the input card.
scenes.html:
Troubleshooting tip
Meter vs. PLC
If they disagree, check the scaling or the input card.
Syon Automation LLC
